reviews.comment: He includes some theorems/topics in his lectures that aren't tested on the exams, but he also makes sure to go over relevant example problems. His homework is sometimes difficult, yet it's doable if you pay attention in class. Class is exam heavy, but understanding the homework and exam study guides  will help you do well on them.

Took Baskin seeing that not many people had reviewed his 308 class so I thought I'd share my two cents. Overall, 308 was a tough class and I had to study a lot (~12-15 hours per test) due to my inability to follow class lectures. Class is theory-heavy, so highly recommend using YT and MLC to practice. Tough class, but Baskin is a pretty chill guy.

Prof Baskins focuses on the theory of math, he doesn't do too many examples. This means you have to attend lectures and pay attention because it is quite hard to follow the class if you do not. The course will be much easier if you have already taken linear algebra. If you are in honors, the homework is quite hard but the exams are easy.

He's very enthusiastic and loves what he teaches. Because your grade relies on very few exams, you'll need to come very prepared. This class focuses more on theorems than just computations. You'll need to be able to explain them and apply them, which can be a rough adjustment at first. The homework, while not mandatory, is really important to do.

One quiz every week. Overall grade is based on quizzes and exams only. 2 midterms and 1 final exam that was cumulative. He is very passionate about math and is willing to work with you so you understand the topics. Cares very much about his students and his teaching. He likes to lecture on the reasons why theorems work rather than lots of examples.

I had to drop this class due to special circumstances, however Professor Baskin is a great professor and knows what hes doing. Our exams were approximately 60% of our grades, and the rest was homework. He is great at conveying what he knows to students and is willing to take time to explain it more thoroughly. If I could take it again I would.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Baskin last year, and didnt have much to say at the time. After taking another Calculus class with a different professor, I realized just how good Dr. Baskin really is. While his lectures are somewhat monotonous, I learned so much and would definitely recommend him. He explains everything and helps you understand each concept.

Prof Baskin is a great calculus professor. If taking 171, don't get bogged down with the abstract explanations he throws at you, he does this not to teach you, but to make you a well-rounded mathematician. He is caring, funny, and understandable, and tests aren't too bad.

Luckily the class material is not difficult. This professor focuses on theorems and definitions with zero examples in lecture. The only examples are provided in your recitation section which is after the homework is due. If there is an option I would take a different professor. Got lucky with an amazing TA.

Good professor if you are well prepared to take CAL 1 however if you have not covered CAL 1 material recently I would not recommend as he goes very fast in lecture and he generally does tough problems in class.
He's really understanding and caring. He literally posts his notes online so you don't even need to go to the class.
Overall a solid professor, focuses mostly on theory and lots of proofs. If the subject material for the course is brand new to you then expect to go to office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class itself was difficult mostly because of the proofs. He mostly wrote proofs and theorems during lectures and they help a bit if you know more about them beforehand. There aren't many examples in class because of how many proofs there are. Homeworks are difficult but go to his office hours/make an appointment for homeworks and attend reviews
Not a good math professor. He just writes down theorems and definitions the whole lecture and doesn't do very good examples or helpful homeworks for the test. I wouldnt recommend for 323

He is one of the better math teachers that I've had at TAMU. He's extremely passionate about the material he teaches and makes lectures as detailed as he can. The class material is horrible, but he is a great professor. There are homeworks every week and he will double up on them after tests (which sucks). Heavy on proofs.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again
